title: Modified Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass in Mice
author: Teri Stevenson
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zchf2t6
materials: Ligate esophagus proximal to stomach using 6-0 silk.
An esophageal-jejunostomy is performed using 8-0 nylon.

steps.title: Prepare Animals Preoperatively
steps.instruction: Prepare the mice for surgery by managing housing, nutrition, and medication.

substeps.instruction: Singly-house all animals.
Remove all bedding from the cages used for housing.
Administer Ensure 12 hours before surgery.
Administer preoperative pain medication: Ketoprofen (5 mg/kg).

steps.title: Induce Anesthesia and Position Mouse
steps.instruction: Prepare the mouse for the surgical procedure.

substeps.instruction: Ensure adequacy of anesthesia.
Place mouse on a surgical board/field over a warm water circulating blanket and immobilize gently.
Prep and drape the animal sterilely.

steps.title: Perform Midline Laparotomy
steps.instruction: Open the abdominal cavity using a midline incision.

substeps.instruction: Make a midline laparotomy incision with sharp surgical scissors, staying on the linea alba and away from the rectus abdominus muscles.

steps.title: Locate and Transect Intestine
steps.instruction: Identify the Ligament of Treitz and perform the initial intestinal transection.

substeps.instruction: Gently sweep intestinal contents using cotton swabs until the Ligament of Treitz is located.
Transect the intestine distal to the ligament.
Close the proximal end using 8-0 nylon.

steps.title: Perform Anastomoses and Ligation
steps.instruction: Create the gastric bypass connections and ligate the esophagus.

substeps.instruction: Perform a jejuno-jejunostomy using a side to side anastomosis.
Ligate the esophagus proximal to the stomach using 6-0 silk.
Perform an esophageal-jejunostomy using 8-0 nylon.

steps.title: Close the Abdomen
steps.instruction: Close the abdominal wall using a two-layer interrupted technique.

substeps.instruction: Suture the first interrupted muscle layer with 6-0 monocryl suture, ensuring connective tissue is sutured and not the muscle proper.
Suture the second skin layer in a simple, interrupted fashion with 7-0 Prolene suture.

steps.title: Immediate Postoperative Care
steps.instruction: Provide immediate recovery support and hydration.

substeps.instruction: Administer 1.0 ml of warmed, sterile saline following the procedure.
Place mice in recovery cages.

steps.title: Postoperative Monitoring and Maintenance
steps.instruction: Manage the recovery environment, diet, and pain for the mice.

substeps.instruction: Keep mouse cages partially on a veterinary-approved heating pad for 5 to 7 days postoperatively.
Maintain mice on an Ensure diet for 48 hours post-surgery with no bedding in the cage.
Administer ketoprofen (5 mg/kg) post-op and again at 24 hours postoperative; provide additional pain medication if needed based on recovery.
Monitor general behavior (bright/alert/responsive vs. depressed/obtunded) until recovered, typically 7-14 days.
